## Why This Is Asked

This question tests end-to-end onboarding automation basics in Azure AD with a beginner-friendly workflow: provisioning, licensing, group-based access, MFA enforcement, and safe validation.

## Key Concepts

- Azure AD user provisioning from CSV via Microsoft Graph API or PowerShell
- License assignment and SKU management
- Security groups for application access control
- Conditional Access policies for MFA enforcement
- Sandbox testing and rollback procedures

## Code Example

```powershell
# Connect to Azure AD
Connect-AzureAD

# Import users from CSV
$users = Import-Csv -Path "./users.csv"

# Create each user
foreach ($user in $users) {
    $passwordProfile = New-Object Microsoft.Open.AzureAD.Model.PasswordProfile
    $passwordProfile.Password = "TemporaryP@ssw0rd!"
    
    New-AzureADUser -DisplayName $user.DisplayName `
        -UserPrincipalName $user.UserPrincipalName `
        -MailNickName $user.MailNickname `
        -PasswordProfile $passwordProfile `
        -AccountEnabled $true
}

# Assign license
$license = Get-AzureADSubscribedSku | Where-Object { $_.SkuPartNumber -eq 'ENTERPRISEPACK' }
$users = Get-AzureADUser
$users | ForEach-Object { Set-AzureADUserLicense -ObjectId $_.ObjectId -AssignedLicenses @{Add=$license} }

# Add users to security groups
$group1 = Get-AzureADGroup -SearchString "App1_Users"
$group2 = Get-AzureADGroup -SearchString "App2_Users"
$users | ForEach-Object {
    Add-AzureADGroupMember -ObjectId $group1.ObjectId -RefObjectId $_.ObjectId
    Add-AzureADGroupMember -ObjectId $group2.ObjectId -RefObjectId $_.ObjectId
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates real-world multi-tenant Azure AD OIDC integration with Vault, emphasizing least privilege, credential revocation, and operational automation.

## Key Concepts
- Azure AD OIDC with a multi-tenant app registration
- Vault auth/oidc method with bound_claims for tenant-to-role mapping
- Namespaces and per-tenant policies for tenant isolation
- Token TTLs, rotation, and automated credential revocation

## Code Example
```hcl
# Vault OIDC role example per tenant
vault write auth/oidc/role/tenant-<tid> \
  bound_audiences="<AAD-Client-Id>" \
  bound_claims={"tid":"<tenant-id>"} \
  user_claim="upn" \
  token_ttl="1h" \
  token_max_ttl="24h" \
  token_policies=["tenant-<tid>-policy"]

# Namespace-scoped policy example
path "namespace/<tenant-id>/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
}
```

## Design Considerations
| Concern | Recommendation |
|---------|----------------|
| Tenant isolation | Separate namespaces with dedicated policies |
| Token lifetime | 15–60 min TTL, 24h max TTL with renewal |
| Rapid revocation | Vault token revoke + Azure AD token invalidation |
| Compromised tenant | Conditional access policies + batch token revocation |
| Sandbox validation | Pre-deployment testing in isolated namespace |
| Rollback | Immediate token revocation + access policy deny-all |
